title: L'alphabet
subtitle: Letters, accents and spelling out loud

path.title: L'alphabet
path.subtitle: Letters, tricky pairs, accents and spelling

letters.trick: A is the sound you make at the doctor: “ahh”.
B = “bay”, like a bay by the sea.
C sounds like “say”. Say C!
D sounds like “day”. D-day!

letters.hint: A soft “uh”, lips a little rounded. Not “ee”!
letters.trick: E is “euh”, the sound French people make when they hesitate: “euh…”.
F = “eff”, same as English.

letters.hint: “zhay”, like the s in “measure”. English J sound, French G!
letters.trick: G and J swap places from English. G = “zhay”, as in girafe.

letters.hint: “ash”. In words, H is silent: homme sounds like “om”.
letters.trick: Hache means axe. The axe chopped H's sound off, so it's silent in words.

letters.hint: Like “ee”. This is the one that sounds like English E.
letters.trick: I = “ee”, like the i in Paris.
J = “zhee”, as in jeudi. Just remember: G and J trade sounds in French.
K = “ka”, like the start of “karate”.

letters.hint: Like “el”. Same as the word elle (she).
letters.trick: L sounds just like elle, the word for she.
M = “em”, same as English.
N = “en”, same as English.
O: make a perfect round O with your lips.
P = “pay”. You pay with P.

letters.hint: Like “kü”: say K, then the French U.
letters.trick: Q = K + the French U. Pucker up after the k.

letters.hint: “air”, with a soft gargle at the back of the throat.
letters.trick: R: gargle softly, like rinsing with mouthwash, but gentle.
S = “ess”, same as English.
T sounds like “tay”, as in a cup of tea with a French accent.

letters.hint: Say “ee”, then round your lips like “oo” without moving your tongue.
letters.trick: U: pucker for a kiss, then try to say “ee”. That's the French U.
V = “vay”, rhymes with bé, cé, dé, pé, té.
The French see two Vs in W, not two Us: double vé.
X = “eeks”. Eek, an X!
Y is the Greek I: i grec. It even looks like an I with arms.
Z is “zède”, like the British “zed”.

accents.name: e accent aigu
accents.hint: Sounds like “ay”. The most common accent.
accents.trick: Aigu goes UP, like your voice going up in “ay!”. Rising accent, rising sound.

accents.name: e accent grave
accents.trick: Grave goes DOWN, like a grave in the ground. Low, open “eh”.

accents.name: e accent circonflexe
accents.hint: Also “eh”. Often a missing s from old French: fête, like “feast”.
accents.trick: The circonflexe is a little hat hiding a lost s: forêt = forest, fête = feast, hôpital = hospital.

accents.name: c cédille
accents.hint: Makes C sound like S before a, o, u.
accents.trick: The cédille is a little tail that softens C into S: garçon, français.

accents.name: e tréma
accents.hint: Two dots: say this vowel separately from the one before it.
accents.trick: The two dots split the vowels apart: Noël is “no-el”, not “nole”.

accents.name: a accent grave
accents.hint: Same sound as a. It changes the meaning: à means “to”, a means “has”.
accents.trick: The accent on à is a signpost: à = to. Without it, a = has.

lines.fr: A, B, C, D, E, F, G
lines.en: Sing it to the tune of Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star.
lines.pr: ah, bay, say, day, uh, eff, zhay
lines.fa: آ، بِه، سِه، دِه، اُ، اِف، ژِه

lines.fr: H, I, J, K, L, M, N, O, P
lines.pr: ash, ee, zhee, kah, el, em, en, oh, pay
lines.fa: آش، ای، ژی، کا، اِل، اِم، اِن، اُ، پِه

lines.fr: Q, R, S, T, U, V
lines.pr: kü, air, ess, tay, ü, vay
lines.fa: کو، اِر، اِس، تِه، او، وِه

lines.fr: Et voilà, je connais mon alphabet !
lines.en: And there, I know my alphabet!
